sources.entry: 🧰 dylanaraps/pure-bash-bible: pure bash alternatives to external processes.

summary.one_liner: A reference book of pure bash snippets that replace external commands like sed, awk, cut, seq and sleep with built-in shell features.
summary.what_it_does: The repository is a documentation-style collection ("bible") of bash techniques for doing common tasks without calling external processes. It is organized into sections such as strings, arrays, loops, file handling, file paths, escape sequences, parameter expansion, brace expansion, conditionals, arithmetic, traps, and internal variables. Many entries give an example function plus sample usage, for example trimming whitespace, splitting strings, percent-encoding, reading files into arrays, getting terminal size and cursor position, converting hex and RGB colors, generating a UUID V4, and printing the date via printf's strftime support. Entries note bash version requirements where relevant (for example bash 4+ or 4.4+). The README says the snippets are linted with shellcheck and that tests exist for applicable snippets, with contribution guidelines in CONTRIBUTING.md. A separate "pure sh bible" for POSIX sh is mentioned at the top of the README.
use_cases: replace sed or awk for simple string edits in a bash script
remove external dependencies from shell scripts
speed up bash scripts that call many external commands
trim whitespace or change string case in bash
get terminal size or cursor position from a bash TUI
look up bash parameter expansion or brace expansion syntax
convert hex colors to RGB and back in shell
print ANSI escape sequences for colors and cursor movement
notable: Covers both common and lesser-known bash built-ins in one reference, with example functions for each task
Each snippet is shellcheck-linted and many are backed by unit tests, per the README
Documents bash-version caveats for features like namerefs, printf strftime and case modification
Includes a companion pure sh (POSIX) version of the book
Originated from work on neofetch and pxltrm, per the README
caveats: Several snippets require bash 4+ or 4.4+, so they will not run on older or non-bash shells
Regex matching depends on the regex engine installed on the user's system, per the README
The UUID generator is explicitly not cryptographically secure
